How the runtime layer must target a resource by its primary identifier.

</td><td>

The runtime property to read for list output and to match against for a `byProperty` lookup. For `byId` and `byKey` this is the identifier property; for `byProperty` it is `runtimeProperty` when set, else the identifier property.

This is the value-carrying property — NOT the request parameter name. The request parameter (e.g. `id`<!-- -->, `calendarId`<!-- -->) is a separate schema-contract concern resolved from the command's parameters.

</td></tr>

The targeting strategy: `byId` emits a JXA `byId(value)` lookup; `byProperty` emits a `whose({ <property>: value })[0]` lookup; `byKey` emits the collection's key specifier applied to the value.
